notes: §1985:XIII.3.6.3 SR1: 'Literal-1 must be a two-character nonnumeric literal.' BindCodeClause refuses a literal whose class is not alphanumeric and, at 85, an identifier operand (the 2002 form); Screen85CodeLiteral refuses at DialectLevel < 2002 a literal whose characters are not two (COBOL2713, the witness: CODE "A"). Probes at --std 85 (classes b, c, d): CODE "AB" and CODE "A""" compile and write AB / A" in the first two positions of each line (§1985:XIII.3.6.4 GR1); "ABC", "" (also COBOL0900), 12, N"AB", WS-C, a bare CODE, CODE twice (COBOL2423), and the 2002 forms CODE IS, X"4142" and "A" & "B" (COBOL0900) are refused. kb/Work PB5475 landed: BindCodeClause reads a figurative constant by the value it denotes (CodeFigurativeCharacters: ALL literal-1 is literal-1; ZERO, SPACE, QUOTE, HIGH-VALUE and LOW-VALUE the one fill character) and Screen85CodeLiteral then asks the two-character rule of that value, so CODE ALL "AB" compiles and writes AB (§1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3 admits a figurative constant wherever a format says literal) and CODE SPACE, one character, is refused COBOL2713 by its length. Witnesses: pb5475_code_all_literal (accepted), pb5475_code_figurative_one_character (refused).

next.reason: 1985: "Literal-1 must be a two-character nonnumeric literal."; 2023: "Literal-1 shall be an alphanumeric literal.". 2023 drops the two-character length requirement; alphanumeric literals of other lengths are now accepted in the CODE clause.
